title: The Interface Scorecard
topic: deep dive into front end ui design. i wanna use
subtitle: Twelve dimensions, each with a written Low / Medium / High descriptor, drawn from twenty talks by working designers, design-system leads, front-end system-design interviewers and AI-build practitioners. Use it to grade an app you already own, then to specify the version that grades higher. Distilled from Jesse Showalter, UI Collective, Ras Mic, Envato Tuts+, Eric Tech, theSeniorDev, uxpeak, Self-Made Web Designer, DesignCode, Dave Ebbelaar, Yashica Jain, AI Foundations, Codex Community and GroundZero.
question: Can you do a deep dive into front end UI design. I wanna use this guide as a rubric to apply to my other projects front ends, and use this guide as a critical review of those apps front ends so that there's a rubric, and it and it is scored high, medium, low. And that enables, the LLM to score where it's at today and then propose a solution that would score highly on the rubric So this needs to be an in-depth guide of building high quality front end UIs.

sources.title: Web Design for Beginners | FREE COURSE
sources.contributed: The only source that teaches manual UI/UX design fundamentals end-to-end — project briefs, wireframes, color theory, typography, the eight-point spacing system, common UI patterns (headers, heroes, buttons, galleries, footers, testimonials, tabs, accordions, forms), and responsive breakpoints — applied to a real Figma project.

sources.title: Real Senior Frontend System Design Interview 2026 (AI Coding Included)
sources.contributed: A full mock senior front-end system-design interview transcript covering requirements gathering, state architecture, performance/caching strategy, and how to credibly answer questions about which AI models, harnesses, and guardrails to use.

sources.title: How I Build INSANELY Beautiful Websites Using Claude Code
sources.contributed: An 8-step, tool-by-tool build process (skills to kill AI slop, plan mode, inspiration images, section-by-section build starting with hero, motion rhythm, responsiveness pass, self-audit score, one-command Hostinger deploy) for turning a default Claude Code output into a premium-feeling site.

sources.title: Build a Full-Stack GenAI Project in 4 Hours (FastAPI, React, Supabase)
sources.contributed: Shows front-end UI work embedded inside a full custom-coded stack: scaffolding React+TS+Tailwind+shadcn/ui, invoking Anthropic's 'front-end design' skill, and iterating on chat UI details (loading states, citation panels, logo padding) via screenshot-annotated prompts.

sources.title: How I Build Insane Three.js Websites With Claude Opus 5
sources.contributed: A concrete AI-assisted design workflow for building striking Three.js/3D landing pages with Claude Code (Opus 5): reference-first prompting, MCP-driven inspiration gathering, effort-level settings, and turning repeatable techniques into reusable skills.

sources.title: Amateur vs Pro UI Design | with examples
sources.contributed: A junior-to-senior critique ladder across login, dashboard, and complex-app screens showing exactly which color, hierarchy, spacing, and contrast choices separate amateur from professional UI.

sources.title: Learn Design Systems: Figma Variables, Components, AI, and More
sources.contributed: The deepest, most skeptical treatment of AI in design-system work: exact math for building token/color scales by hand, the case for why AI cannot build tokens or components correctly, and a measured workaround (per-grouping skills) that still only gets ~80-85% there.

sources.title: Design with AI - Full Guide (Tools, Workflows, Design Systems)
sources.contributed: A hands-on, token/time-benchmarked comparison of AI design tools (Grok, Claude Fable/Opus, Codex, Figma AI, Stitch, paper.design) plus a staged AI workflow (iterate → prototype/QA → sync to design system) and a taxonomy of Claude/Figma skills.

sources.title: Building beautiful UI using AI (My design workflow)
sources.contributed: A concrete, repeatable workflow for generating a consistent design system and tokens with AI (Claude Design) and porting it into an AI coding agent (Claude Code) so every generated page matches.

sources.title: Build AMAZING Websites Using Claude Code! (Full Guide)
sources.contributed: The only video showing a fully no-code pipeline where an AI (Claude Design) generates an entire visual design system — colors, typography, components, wireframes — from a five-question brand brief, then Claude Code builds and deploys it.

sources.title: The Best AI Automation Stack to Learn in 2026
sources.contributed: Names the specific front-end stack (React + Vite + shadcn/ui) recommended for building AI-automation UIs, and frames the claim that AI has largely solved front-end coding while UX/design taste remains a human bottleneck.

sources.title: How to Be A Web Designer in 2026 (Free Resources & My Best Advice)
sources.contributed: A beginner-facing roadmap covering the four skills (dev, brand, UX, marketing) needed to charge more than a couple hundred dollars per site, with concrete rules of thumb (60-30-10, contrast ratios, SEO structure) rather than AI-tool comparisons.

sources.title: Figma Website Design Tutorial 2026
sources.contributed: The only video where a human manually builds the design system inside a dedicated design tool: naming type styles, defining color variables, constructing button components with variants, and using auto layout for responsive sections — then migrates the file into Wix Studio.

sources.title: Use AI Like a Senior Designer (3 Workflows)
sources.contributed: Three concrete workflows senior designers at Meta/Google actually use: widget-first generation before page generation, persona-driven AI flow testing, and AI-assisted reading-order for developer handoff.

sources.title: How to Systematically Setup LLM Evals (Metrics, Unit Tests, LLM-as-a-Judge)
sources.contributed: Not about front-end UI design at all — a crash course on evaluating LLM/agent applications (unit tests, human/LLM-judge alignment, A/B testing); contributes no citable UI-design claims to this guide.

sources.title: Data Scientist to AI Engineer Roadmap for 2026
sources.contributed: Frames front-end/full-stack skill as one step in a six-part AI-engineer roadmap and names it the area data scientists find least familiar; contributes career-sequencing context rather than concrete UI technique.

sources.title: Top UI/UX Design Tips - How to Design a Great Bottom Mobile Navigation Bar
sources.contributed: A checklist of concrete, numeric UI specs (icon sizes, tap targets, tab counts, contrast ratios) specifically for designing a mobile bottom navigation bar.

sources.title: 14 Front End System Design Concepts | Explained in 10 Minutes
sources.contributed: The engineering side of front end: rendering strategy choice, re-render/caching/pagination techniques that make a UI fast, independent of how it looks.

sources.title: These UI libraries + AI = beautiful looking web apps
sources.contributed: A rapid-fire tour of nine free component/template libraries plus the one workflow trick that matters: download a component you like, then have your AI agent extract a design system from it.

sources.title: The Never Ending Lore of Harness | Vivek Trivedy (Product Lead, Langchain)
sources.contributed: How to configure the AI coding agent itself (prompting, verification hooks, file-system context, sub-agent sizing) that a designer relies on when generating and iterating UI code with tools like Claude Code.

gaps: No corpus video discusses accessibility (WCAG contrast/keyboard navigation/screen-reader support) for any of the interfaces built.
No guidance on mobile-first design or touch-target sizing beyond ad hoc per-viewport adjustments made after the fact in Wix Studio.
No discussion of page-speed, Core Web Vitals, or front-end performance budgeting for any of the shipped sites.
No usability or user testing methodology is shown — all design decisions are validated by the builder's own eye, never by watching a real user.
No systematic rationale for a typographic scale or spacing grid (e.g., a ratio system or 8-point grid) beyond ad hoc pixel choices like 36px/24px headings.
No treatment of dark mode or multi-theme support in any of the design systems built.
No cost/time benchmark exists for the manual Figma-build path comparable to the detailed Claude+Hostinger cost table, so a reader can't directly compare no-code vs. hand-crafted design economics.
No discussion of design handoff to developers when the designer and coder are different people/teams (all examples are one person doing both roles, often via AI).
No source covers accessibility beyond basic color-contrast checking — no guidance on ARIA, keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, or focus management.

No source explains how a finished Figma design or an AI-cloned reference actually gets translated into production HTML/CSS/component code, or what a design-to-dev handoff process looks like in practice.
No source compares component/design-system tooling beyond a single mention of shadcn/ui — no discussion of design tokens, Storybook, or maintaining a design system at scale.
No source discusses user testing, usability testing, or validating a UI design with real users before shipping.
No source gives any data connecting specific design decisions (color, layout, copy) to measurable business outcomes like conversion rate or engagement.
The AI-driven workflow videos (G-F5Qvy-7KM, omU3zR3K7-U) don't explain how to evaluate whether an AI-generated design is actually usable/accessible, only whether it looks distinctive ('non-slop').

No source covers motion/animation design principles systematically — the Three.js video shows effects (weather, cloth, orbiting) as anecdotal outcomes without a framework for when/how much motion to use.

No source addresses design work for non-marketing UI (e.g., dense data tables, enterprise dashboards, forms with complex validation) — B-ytMSuwbf8's patterns are all marketing/portfolio-site oriented.
No concrete accessibility guidance (contrast ratios, screen reader patterns, keyboard navigation specifics) beyond a single passing mention of 'optimize for mobile and accessibilities.'
No coverage of responsive/mobile-specific layout patterns or breakpoints for the UI designs critiqued.
No typography guidance beyond token category names (display size, H1/H2/H3) — no advice on font pairing, line height, or reading measure.
No motion/animation design principles (easing curves, durations, when to animate) beyond naming a couple of example micro-interactions (BUI accordion bounce, tilt card).
No discussion of design-to-dev handoff process, versioning of a design system over time, or how teams keep a design system in sync as it evolves post-launch.
No data tying specific design decisions (color, hierarchy, spacing) to measurable outcomes like conversion rate or task completion time — critique in the corpus is qualitative/visual only.
No evaluation or comparison of specific component libraries/CSS frameworks (e.g. Tailwind, shadcn) beyond a single passing name-drop of 'BUI.'
No guidance on how to price, pitch, or present this kind of UI work to clients, despite the corpus repeatedly referencing freelance/agency and portfolio contexts.

None of the four videos give concrete subscription pricing or a cost-per-design comparison across the AI tools they benchmark (Grok, Claude Fable/Opus, Codex, paper.design) — only relative token/time figures, so a reader can't build an actual budget from this corpus alone.
Native mobile app design systems (iOS/Android-specific component libraries, platform HIG differences) are not covered — only responsive 'mobile optimized' variants of web components are addressed.
There's no guidance on multi-designer or team collaboration workflows when several people are prompting AI against the same shared design system at once.

Accessibility testing coverage stops at contrast ratios (Chrome DevTools) and Claude's built-in accessibility-review skill — no specific screen-reader software or manual testing protocol is discussed.
No video addresses versioning or migrating design tokens across breaking changes/app releases once a system is in production.
AI-generated logo or illustration quality for branding work is never benchmarked — all AI-quality comparisons in this cluster are about UI screens/dashboards, not brand assets.
No corpus content on choosing a specific color system (hex values, palette-generation method) beyond naming 'design tokens' and 'brand palette' as concepts.
No guidance on desktop or tablet primary navigation patterns — wLJ40GV2XEc is scoped entirely to mobile bottom navigation.
No concrete detail on how to raise a website's 'trust and conversion' score once a self-audit flags it low (bkTY9gYkWis's own audit scored trust 3/10 with no follow-up fix shown).
No cost or time benchmarks for the AI design workflows described (e.g. how long widget-generation exploration takes, how much the Claude Code / Codex / image-generation combo costs per project).
No discussion of design-system tooling implementation (e.g. Storybook) beyond a passing mention that it's worth considering.
No comparison of how the persona-driven AI flow-testing prompt performs across different coding-agent tools beyond one Google Antigravity demo.
No guidance on accessibility beyond reading order and nav contrast ratios — no coverage of keyboard navigation, ARIA patterns, or screen-reader testing workflows.
